content.title: When Everything Feels Too Much
content.scope: A Little More Room · Eight brief educational readings, with optional everyday practices. These are not diagnosis or treatment.

intent.subject: When Everything Feels Too Much
intent.direction: Explore a practical psychological perspective with ordinary examples and realistic limits.
intent.perspective: Public education; gentle, optional practices without clinical promises.

readings.label: You can begin gently
readings.text: Welcome to A Little More Room, from Orbforma. When everything asks for your attention at once, you do not have to solve it all immediately. Today, we explore a small grounding practice.
readings.learn: Welcome to A Little More Room, from Orbforma. When everything asks for your attention at once, you do not have to solve it all immediately. Today, we explore a small grounding practice.

visualBrief.subject: You can begin gently
visualBrief.context: An everyday illustration of this optional practice.

readings.label: Choose one ordinary object
readings.text: If you would like, look at one ordinary object nearby. A cup, a leaf, or the edge of a table will do. Notice its color and shape. Your eyes can stay open.
readings.learn: If you would like, look at one ordinary object nearby. A cup, a leaf, or the edge of a table will do. Notice its color and shape. Your eyes can stay open.

readings.label: Find a comfortable anchor
readings.text: You might notice the chair supporting you, or a familiar sound in the room. Choose whatever feels comfortable. If paying attention to your body feels unpleasant, an outside object is enough.
readings.learn: You might notice the chair supporting you, or a familiar sound in the room. Choose whatever feels comfortable. If paying attention to your body feels unpleasant, an outside object is enough.

readings.placementReason: A practical elaboration of the introductory perspective.

readings.label: Name it without judging
readings.text: Perhaps you feel overwhelmed, restless, or tired. A simple description can be enough. You do not need to turn this moment into a judgment about your character or your entire life.
readings.learn: Perhaps you feel overwhelmed, restless, or tired. A simple description can be enough. You do not need to turn this moment into a judgment about your character or your entire life.

visualBrief.subject: Name it without judging
visualBrief.context: An everyday illustration of this optional practice.

readings.placementReason: A practical elaboration of the introductory perspective.

readings.label: Let breathing stay natural
readings.text: There is no special breathing pattern to get right. Let your breath continue naturally. You can simply notice the light or listen to a sound. Feeling perfectly calm is not the assignment.
readings.learn: There is no special breathing pattern to get right. Let your breath continue naturally. You can simply notice the light or listen to a sound. Feeling perfectly calm is not the assignment.

visualBrief.context: An everyday illustration of this optional practice.

readings.placementReason: A practical elaboration of the introductory perspective.

readings.label: Return to one practical thing
readings.text: Imagine an inbox full of messages. After noticing your surroundings, you might choose one message that needs an answer. Grounding does not clear the inbox; it offers a place to begin.
readings.learn: Imagine an inbox full of messages. After noticing your surroundings, you might choose one message that needs an answer. Grounding does not clear the inbox; it offers a place to begin.

readings.label: You are allowed to stop
readings.text: If an exercise makes you more uncomfortable, stop. Look around, change position, or speak with someone supportive. Choosing a different approach is useful information, not a failure to do the practice correctly.
readings.learn: If an exercise makes you more uncomfortable, stop. Look around, change position, or speak with someone supportive. Choosing a different approach is useful information, not a failure to do the practice correctly.

readings.label: Choose your next small step
readings.text: Choose one manageable next step, whether that is a break, a small task, or asking for help. This is education, not treatment. Persistent, worsening, or disruptive distress deserves professional support.
